title: Data Analysis Protocol for Mapping Mangrove Forests Using Drones
author: Monika Ruwaimana
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qh7dt9n
materials: Download and install free software GeoSetter from http://www.geosetter.de/en/ . Open the GeoSetter. On the upper left directory dropdown, select the folder containing the drone images. On the bottom right, click the icon open and open the .gpx file from the previous step. A Google map on the upper right window will show the drone track. a
Install Agisoft Photoscan Professional with license.
Minimize the QGIS. Open software called OSGeo4WShell, which is installed together with QGIS. a
Type otbgui_ComputeOGRLayersFeaturesStatistics and press enter. a
Type otbgui_TrainOGRLayersClassifier and press enter a
Type otbgui_OGRLayeClassifier and press enter. a
Download the Pontius Matrix Excel file from http://www2.clarku.edu/~rpontius/PontiusMatrix41.xlsx

steps.title: Extract and Upload Flight Logs
steps.instruction: Retrieve flight log data from the Flytrex device and upload it to the Flytrex platform.

substeps.instruction: Remove the memory card from the Flytrex device and copy the .fvp flight log files to a computer.
Sign in to flytrex.com, navigate to the profile page, click 'Upload Mission', and upload the .fvp file.

steps.title: Export and Format Flight Data
steps.instruction: Export the mission data to CSV and clean the file in Microsoft Excel.

substeps.instruction: On the uploaded mission, click the drop-down arrow next to the country flag, select 'Export Mission', and choose 'Download CSV'.
Open the .csv file in Microsoft Excel and delete all columns except latitude, longitude, altitude feet, and datetime.
Split the datetime column into separate date and time columns.
Adjust the GMT time to local time (e.g., add 8 hours for Malaysia GMT+8).
Save and close the Excel file.

steps.title: Convert CSV to GPX
steps.instruction: Convert the cleaned flight data into GPX format using an online converter.

substeps.instruction: Open the .csv file with Notepad, select all text, and copy it.
Go to gpsvisualizer.com, select 'Convert to GPX', and paste the text into the data window.
Set the 'Plain text delimiter' to comma and click 'Convert'.
Download the resulting .gpx data.

steps.title: Geotag Images in Agisoft
steps.instruction: Synchronize drone images with the GPX flight data to assign coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Select an image from the middle of the image list and find the corresponding record (matching minutes and seconds) in the 'Tracks' window.
Press Ctrl-A to select all images.
Go to menu 'Images' > 'Synchronize with GPS data file' (or press Ctrl-G), click 'OK', and then 'Yes' on the pop-up.
Verify coordinates appear for each image and click the save icon.

steps.title: Initial Low-Resolution Model Generation
steps.instruction: Generate a preliminary 3D model in Agisoft using low-quality settings for speed.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Workflow' > 'Add Photos' and select all geotagged images.
Go to 'Workflow' > 'Align photos', set Accuracy to 'Low', and click 'OK'.
Go to 'Workflow' > 'Build Dense Cloud', set Quality to 'Low', and click 'OK'.
Go to 'Workflow' > 'Build Mesh', set Face count to 'Low', and click 'OK'.
Go to 'Workflow' > 'Build Texture' and click 'OK'.

steps.title: Create Ground Control Points (GCPs)
steps.instruction: Establish at least 5 control points using Google Earth to improve accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Open Google Earth and locate a distinct feature in the study area.
In Agisoft, right-click the corresponding point on the image and select 'Create Marker' (creates 'point 1').
In Google Earth, place a mark over the same point and copy the latitude and longitude (decimal degree format) into the Agisoft Markers Panel.
Repeat until at least 5 control points are generated.

steps.title: Final High-Resolution Model Generation
steps.instruction: Re-align and rebuild the model using higher quality settings based on computer capacity.

substeps.instruction: In the 'Reference' panel (upper left), select all cameras, right-click, and choose 'Reset Camera Alignment', then click 'Yes'.
Repeat the 'Workflow' sequence (Align Photos $\rightarrow$ Build Texture) using 'Medium' or 'High' settings.
Note: Medium settings take ~6 hours and High settings ~20 hours on a 2.6GHz processor with 8GB RAM (this research used Medium).

steps.title: Export Orthophoto and DEM
steps.instruction: Export the final processed products from Agisoft.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'File' > 'Export Orthophoto' > 'Export JPEG/TIF'. Set coordinate system to WGS 84/UTM zone 48N, set Pixel size to 0.05 (5cm resolution), tick 'Write World file', and export.
Go to 'File' > 'Export DEM' > 'Export TIFF/BIL'. Set coordinate system to WGS 84/UTM zone 48N, set Pixel size to 0.05 (5cm resolution), tick 'Write World file', and export.

steps.title: Prepare QGIS Environment
steps.instruction: Install and configure QGIS with necessary plugins.

substeps.instruction: Download and install QGIS OSGeo4W advanced package (including ORFEO Toolbox and SAGA GIS) from qgis.org.
Open QGIS and select 'Advanced Interface' in the 'Processing Toolbox' panel (bottom left).

steps.title: Import and Optimize Raster Layers
steps.instruction: Load the exported images and optimize them for performance.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Layer' > 'Add Layer' > 'Add Raster Layer' (or Ctrl-Shift-R) and load the RGB, IR, and DEM mosaic images.
For each image, right-click > 'Properties' > 'Pyramids' tab, select all resolutions, and click 'Apply' to speed up zooming.

steps.title: Align and Georeference IR Image
steps.instruction: Ensure the IR and RGB images overlap perfectly; georeference if necessary.

substeps.instruction: Check overlap by toggling tick boxes in the 'Layers Panel' and adjusting 'Global transparency' in 'Properties' > 'Transparency'.
If not overlapped, go to 'Raster' > 'Georeferencer' > 'File' > 'Open Raster' and select the IR image.
Add at least 3 reference points (7-8 used in this research) by clicking a landmark on the IR image and selecting 'From map canvas' to pick the corresponding point on the RGB image.
Go to 'Setting' > 'Transformation Setting', choose a transformation type (Polynomial is recommended), specify the output filename, and click 'OK'.

steps.title: Merge Raster Layers
steps.instruction: Combine the IR, RGB, and DEM images into a single merged file.

substeps.instruction: In the Processing Toolbox, search for and open 'GDAL Merge'.
Select all images (IR, RGB, DEM) as input layers and tick 'Layer Stack'.
Specify the output filename and click 'Run' (process takes ~1-2 hours).
Build pyramids for the new merged image as described in the optimization step.

steps.title: Final Georeferencing and Visualization
steps.instruction: Georeference the merged image against a satellite image and set band visualizations.

substeps.instruction: Georeference the merged image using a Satellite Image as the reference (following the Georeferencer steps). Build pyramids for the result.
Load the merged/georeferenced image into QGIS and create a duplicate via right-click > 'Duplicate'.
For the original image: 'Properties' > 'Style' > 'Multiband color'. Set Bands 5-6-7 (R, G, B) for true color, set contrast to 'No Enhancement', and apply.
For the duplicate image: 'Properties' > 'Style' > 'Singleband pseudocolor'. Set Band 1 (DEM) with values 0-30m, click 'Classify', and apply.

steps.title: Crop Invalid Areas
steps.instruction: Remove parallax and invalid DEM areas using a mask polygon.

substeps.instruction: Compare the true color and DEM images to identify parallax/invalid areas.
Click 'New Shapefile Layer', select 'polygon' type and UTM Zone 48 coordinate system. Name it '03clip'.
Use 'Toggle Editing' and 'Add feature' to draw a polygon excluding the invalid areas, then save.
Go to 'Raster' > 'Extraction' > 'Clipper'. Use the merged image as input, select 'Mask Layer' as '03clip', and export. Repeat for the Satellite Image.
Optional: For large images, add '--config GDAL_CACHEMAX 1000 -wm 1000' to the Clipper script to increase cache to 1000Mb.

steps.title: ROI Creation and Signature Generation
steps.instruction: Use the Semi-Automatic Classification Plugin (SCP) to create training regions of interest (ROIs).

substeps.instruction: Install 'Semi-Automatic Classification Plugin' via 'Plugins' > 'Manage and Install Plugin' and activate it.
Load the clipped raster into the SCP plugin using the refresh button.
In 'SCP: ROI creation' panel, click 'New shp' (e.g., 'traindroneS'), assign a class ID (e.g., '1') and name (e.g., 'water'), and uncheck 'Add. Sig list'.
Use 'Create ROI Polygon' to draw polygons of equal size over the image and click 'Save ROI'.
Repeat for all classes using field survey data and photographs. Load plot data via 'Layer' > 'Add Layer' > 'Add delimited Text Layer' (e.g., 'AT plot.csv').
Select all ROIs and click 'Add to signature' (takes 20-30 mins for drone, 2-3 mins for satellite).
In 'SCP: Classification' panel, save the signature file (e.g., 'sigdroneall') and click 'Create signature plot' to evaluate class separation.

steps.title: Prepare Training/Validation Subsets
steps.instruction: Split the ROI data into training (A) and validation (B) sets.

substeps.instruction: Save 'traindroneS' as five separate files: 'traindroneS1A' through 'traindroneS5A'.
Use 'Vector' > 'Research Tools' > 'Random Selection Within Subsets' on 'traindroneS1A' with 'C_ID' as unique ID and 50% percentage.
Save the selected features as 'traindroneS1B'.
Delete the selected polygons from 'traindroneS1A' to create a non-overlapping pair. Repeat for all 5 sets.

steps.title: Object-Based Segmentation
steps.instruction: Perform mean-shift segmentation to group pixels into objects.

substeps.instruction: In Processing Toolbox, run 'Exact Large-Scale Mean-Shift segmentation, step 1' on the clipped raster ('03clip'), allocating available RAM (standard 128 Mb).
Run 'step 2' using the 'Filtered output' from step 1 to get an 'Output image'.
Run 'step 3' using '03clip' as input and the 'Output image' as segmented image. Save as '03droneseg'.
Repeat this entire segmentation process for the satellite image.

steps.title: Manual Rule-Based Classification
steps.instruction: Classify segments based on visual judgment and spectral rules.

substeps.instruction: Open '03droneseg' properties > 'Style' > 'Rule Based'. Write rules for features (e.g., water, land) and refine based on visual judgment.
Open the Attribute Table and use the Field Calculator to create a text/string field 'classS'.
Enter the logic (e.g., CASE WHEN "meanB1" > 120 AND "meanB0" = 12... THEN 'RA' ... END).
Use the Field Calculator again to assign integer codes to these classes for accuracy analysis.

steps.title: Automatic OGR Classification
steps.instruction: Train and apply an OGR model for automatic classification using the OSGeo4W Shell.

substeps.instruction: In QGIS, use 'Join attributes by location' (batch process) to join '03satseg' with paired training files (trainsat1A-1B to 5A-5B) using 'contains', 'equal', 'touches', 'overlaps', and 'within'.
Use Table Manager to delete 'MC_ID', 'MC_info', and 'C_info' and rename 'classID' to 'class'.
In OSGeo4W Shell, use ComputeOGR to generate an XML file ('03satseg.xml') for the input shapefile using features 'meanB0' to 'meanB6'.
Generate XML files for each training shapefile (e.g., 'orgsat1A.xml').
Use TrainOGR to create model files (e.g., 'orgsat1A.model') using the shapefiles and their corresponding XMLs.
Apply the models to '03satseg' to create predicted class fields (e.g., 'class1A' through 'class5B').

steps.title: Post-Process Automatic Classification
steps.instruction: Dissolve and rasterize the automatic classification results.

substeps.instruction: Use 'Polygon dissolve (by attribute)' in batch process on '03satseg' using attributes 'class1A' to 'class5B'. Save as 'SOA1A' to 'SOA5B'.
Use 'Rasterize (vector to raster)' in batch process on 'SOA1A' to 'SOA5B'. Set horizontal and vertical values to 1000 (3000 for drone). Save as .tif files.
Repeat dissolve and conversion for manual-rule results.

steps.title: Spectral Classification (ML and SAM)
steps.instruction: Perform Maximum Likelihood (ML) and Spectral Angle Mapping (SAM) classifications.

substeps.instruction: In SCP, load 'traindroneS1A' and click 'Add to signature'. Save as 'sigdrone1A.xml'.
Select 'Maximum Likelihood' algorithm and 'Perform Classification'. Save as 'DSPML1A'.
Repeat using 'Spectral Angle Mapping' and save as 'DSPSAM1A'.
Repeat the process for all ROI sets (1B through 5B).

steps.title: Accuracy Assessment
steps.instruction: Evaluate classification accuracy using error matrices and Pontius software.

substeps.instruction: In SCP, go to 'Post Processing'. Select the classification result (e.g., 'DSOM') and a reference training site (e.g., 'traindroneS1A') using 'C_ID'.
Calculate the Error Matrix and save as 'DSOM1A' (also exported as .csv).
Test Manual rules with each ROI; test Automatic/ML/SAM using complementary files (e.g., 1A tested by 1B).
Rename categories in the Sample Count tab to class names (water, land, etc.) and paste the matrix into Pontius.
In QGIS, use the 'r.report' algorithm on the classified map ('DSOM') with 'cell count' as the unit. Copy these counts into the Pontius matrix.
Analyze 'Figures Data' (Quantity, Exchange, Shift) and 'Category Component' to identify over/underestimated classes.
